description: Weibull distribution cumulative distribution function 1 - exp(-(x/lambda)^k) (shape k, scale lambda)

tolerance.reason: x, k and lambda are exact doubles and lambda is a power of two, so x/lambda is exact and only t = (x/lambda)^k must be rounded (pow is within an ulp or so in any good libm), then -expm1(-t) is within an ulp. The condition number in t, t / (e^t - 1), is at most 1, so a careful method loses a few ulps at most. 1e-13 as for the other functions; results below 2.2e-308 are judged relative to that number (conventions)

grid: shape k in {0.1, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.1, 3.5, 10, 100} x scale lambda = 2^m for m in {-500, -10, 0, 10, 500} x x = u lambda with u the double nearest t^(1/k) for t in {1e-300, 1e-100, 1e-20, 1e-10, 1e-5, 1e-3, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 37, 50, 100, 300, 700, 708.5, 740, 745.5, 1e3, 1e10, 1e300}, kept where u and x are normal and finite (so x/lambda = u exactly), plus x = 0 and x = -lambda; F is 0 for x <= 0 and rounds to 1 above about t = 37.4
